summary.text: Oba Orhogbua carried Benin’s wars west along the lagoons and made the Awori island a Benin war camp, Eko. Ashipa, remembered in Benin as Orhogbua’s son or grandson, became its first ruler, founding the dynasty whose Obas still reign in Lagos. Lagos paid tribute to Benin until about 1830.

routes.label: Orhogbua’s war canoes go west along the lagoons

moments.title: The war camp
moments.text: The Benin army camps on the island. Benin tradition takes the name Eko from the Edo for a war camp.

moments.title: Ashipa, first ruler of Lagos
moments.text: Ashipa is installed, and Edo chiefs found the lineages that serve the new court. The tribute to Benin lasts until about 1830.
